title: Boss: the resilient order call
summary: Idempotent order creation, a resilient catalogue client, and trace ids that survive everything.

steps.title: The brief
body: Acme's integration creates orders and looks up books. Partners retry, the catalogue has bad days, and support needs
trace ids. You build the three pieces that make the integration boringly reliable.

steps.title: Idempotent order creation
prompt: - `IdempotentOrders(Func<string, (int Status, string Body)> create)`: `create(body)` really creates the order;
- `(int Status, string Body, bool Replayed) Post(string? idempotencyKey, string body)`:

- a new key → call `create`, store the key with the body and the result, return it with `Replayed = false`. Store only results with status below 500, so a failed attempt can be retried with the same key;
- a known key with the **same** body → the stored result with `Replayed = true` (don't call `create`);
- a known key with a **different** body → `(422, "{\"code\":\"IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED\"}", false)`.
starter: public IdempotentOrders(Func<string, (int Status, string Body)> create) { }
public (int Status, string Body, bool Replayed) Post(string? idempotencyKey, string body)
solution: readonly Func<string, (int Status, string Body)> create;
readonly Dictionary<string, (string Request, int Status, string Body)> seen = new();
public IdempotentOrders(Func<string, (int Status, string Body)> create) => this.create = create;
public (int Status, string Body, bool Replayed) Post(string? idempotencyKey, string body)
return prior.Request == body ? (prior.Status, prior.Body, true) : (422, "{\"code\":\"IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED\"}", false);
hints: Store `(request body, status, response body)` per key.
Check the stored request body to tell a retry from a reused key.
template: Dojo.Eq("only one order was created", 1, dojoCreated);
Dojo.Eq("same key, different body", (422, "{\"code\":\"IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED\"}", false), dojoOrders.Post("k1", "{\"isbn\":\"2\"}"));
Dojo.Eq("so the retry with the same key creates the order", (201, "{\"orderId\":\"A2\"}", false), dojoOrders.Post("k2", "{\"isbn\":\"3\"}"));

steps.title: A resilient catalogue client
prompt: The tests declare `IClock` / `FakeClock`. Combine a retry and a breaker into `class CatalogueClient`:
- `CatalogueClient(Func<string, int> backend, IClock clock)`: `backend(isbn)` returns a status (`0` = timeout);
- if the breaker is open (it opened less than `10000` ms ago) → `(503, 0)` without calling;
- otherwise try up to **3** attempts; retry on `0`, `502`, `503`, `504`, sleeping `100` then `200` ms (`clock.Sleep`);
- the **call** (all its attempts) counts as one failure for the breaker if it ends in `0` or `>= 500`; after **2** failed calls in a row the breaker opens; any other outcome resets the count;
- after the cool-down, a call is allowed through again (half-open is not needed here: just reset the count when it succeeds).
- return the final status and attempts used.
starter: public CatalogueClient(Func<string, int> backend, IClock clock) { }
public (int Status, int Attempts) Get(string isbn) => (500, 0);
solution: public CatalogueClient(Func<string, int> backend, IClock clock)
public (int Status, int Attempts) Get(string isbn)
if (openedAt is long t && clock.NowMs - t < 10000) return (503, 0);
var transient = status is 0 or 502 or 503 or 504;
hints: Write the retry loop first, then count the whole call's outcome for the breaker.
Store `openedAt` as a `long?`; clear it when the cool-down has passed.
template: var dojoClient = new CatalogueClient(isbn => { dojoCalls++; return dojoScript.Count > 0 ? dojoScript.Dequeue() : 200; }, dojoClock);
Dojo.Eq("slept 100, 100, 200 so far", new List<int> { 100, 100, 200 }, dojoClock.Sleeps);
Dojo.Eq("no backend call while open", 9, dojoCalls);
Dojo.Eq("after the cool-down calls go through", (200, 1), dojoClient.Get("6"));
public long NowMs { get; private set; }
public void Sleep(int ms) { Sleeps.Add(ms); NowMs += ms; }
public void Advance(int ms) => NowMs += ms;

steps.title: Trace ids that survive
prompt: Write `(string TraceId, Dictionary<string, string> Outbound, string ErrorBody) Trace(Dictionary<string, string> incoming, string exchangeId, string errorCode)`:
- `TraceId`: the incoming `X-Trace-Id` header (any case) if it is 8 to 64 characters of letters, digits and `-`; otherwise `exchangeId` (never trust a malformed id: it ends up in logs);
- `Outbound`: the headers to send to the backend: **only** `X-Trace-Id` (case-insensitive dictionary), whatever arrived;
starter: (string TraceId, Dictionary<string, string> Outbound, string ErrorBody) Trace(Dictionary<string, string> incoming, string exchangeId, string errorCode)
solution: (string TraceId, Dictionary<string, string> Outbound, string ErrorBody) Trace(Dictionary<string, string> incoming, string exchangeId, string errorCode)
var traceId = given != null && Regex.IsMatch(given, "^[A-Za-z0-9-]{8,64}$") ? given : exchangeId;
var outbound = new Dictionary<string, string>(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase) { ["X-Trace-Id"] = traceId };
return (traceId, outbound, JsonSerializer.Serialize(new { code = errorCode, traceId }));
hints: Find the header case-insensitively; the tests pass an ordinary dictionary.
template: Dojo.Eq("keeps a well-formed incoming id", "6f2c81d4-aa", dojoA.TraceId);
Dojo.Eq("only the trace id goes to the backend", "X-Trace-Id=6f2c81d4-aa", string.Join(";", dojoA.Outbound.Select(kv => kv.Key + "=" + kv.Value)));
Dojo.Eq("no incoming id -> exchange id", "ex-12345", Trace(new(), "ex-12345", "X").TraceId);
Dojo.Eq("malformed id is replaced", "ex-12345", Trace(new() { ["X-Trace-Id"] = "bad id\nINJECTED log line" }, "ex-12345", "X").TraceId);
